articleTitle: Bending Losses Prediction on G652 and G657 Optical Fibers through Marcuse Formula
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The huge demand for data communication has massively made the use of optical fibers that offer more advantages than other transmission lines, such as high-speed data transmission and robustness to interferences. Deploying a fiber optic cable should consider some conditions, such as coupling and bending. Some conditions require cables to be bent extremely small, such as when a cable must be connected through small spaces, pillars and corners. This bending loss can contribute to the total loss in transmission, which is much higher than macro bending. This research investigates power transmission loss of G652 and G657 optical fibers through the Marcuse Formula and also considers experiments from previous results. The observed parameter is losses due to turns and variations in wavelengths and bending radius. G652 fiber optic cable has a greater bending loss value than type G657 when the condition of the wavelength, bending radius, and the number of turns are the same. Bending loss achieves the highest results when the wavelength value is 1550 nm with 3 turns and a bending radius of 0.5 cm on the G657 optical fiber. The calculated results show comparable results with previous experiments. It shows that G652 has lower losses due to G657 due to the refractive indices differences. The Marcuse formula can be used to predict the micro-bending loss of optical fibers.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Lung Sound Using YAMNet for Identifying Lung Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The identification of lung sounds is crucial in the fields of health and medicine. In this research, a deep learning architecture is applied to identify various types of lung diseases based on lung sounds. The proposed technique utilizes YAMNet for feature extraction from audio data. The Mel spectrograms generated from these features are used for multi-class audio classification, enabling the identification of different lung sound types. The study's comprehensive dataset consists of 1132 audio samples from 5 classes of lung sounds, providing a diverse and representative collection for training and evaluation. This model, trained and tested using an optimized “Adam” optimizer, achieved an accuracy of 81,54%. Using a varied fold crossvalidation technique, the model attained an average accuracy of 76,67% over 500 epochs. The research yielded accuracy values of 85.47%, precision of 65.96%, recall of 54.35%, and an F1- score of 58.98%. Additionally, the datasets used in this research were obtained from Kaggle and the ICHBI 2017 challenge, ensuring robust and validated source data.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network for Melanoma Skin Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Melanoma skin cancer is a global health concern due to its life-threatening nature and visual similarity to benign skin conditions. Accurate melanoma identification requires specialized expertise, which is often scarce and expensive. This scarcity highlights the critical need for accessible and cost-effective diagnostic solutions. Leveraging deep learning, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach rooted in computer vision, offers a promising avenue for melanoma detection. This study utilizes Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithms, particularly DenseNet121 and VGG19 architecture, to develop robust melanoma classification models. Through rigorous evaluation, DenseNet121 emerges as the optimal architecture, achieving an impressive accuracy of 0.9385 and a minimal loss of 0.1497. Furthermore, we demonstrate practical implementation by deploying the DenseNet121 model in a web-based application using the Flask framework. Our findings underscore the efficacy of deep learning in melanoma detection and highlight the feasibility of translating such advancements into user-friendly diagnostic tools, addressing the urgent need for accessible healthcare solutions in melanoma management.

articleTitle: Development of Gamification for Student Participation Management Information System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Gamification is a concept that applies game elements to systems that do not contain game elements, such as systems in the fields of education, business, and health. Game elements that are applied can be in the form of points, levels, leaderboards, badges, challenges/quests etc. The purpose of gamification is to increase a value, such as increasing user motivation, attracting users, or to improve service quality. One of the problems faced by campuses in Indonesia is the low participation of students in participating in activities held at the faculty or university, such as questionnaire, public lectures, seminars, and workshops. To overcome this problem, it is necessary to trigger student motivation to participate in activities, in the form of giving points to students who participate in activities. This can be realized by applying the concept of gamification to student participation. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct research to design the implementation of gamification of student participation activities based on cases of low student participation in participating in activities at campus. This research is implemented in a student participation management information system. The research begins by identifying the problems that become the background of research and studies of previous studies regarding the implementation of gamification in software. This research was conducted using the waterfall software development method, which consists of the identification stage of system requirements, the system design stage, the code implementation stage, and the system testing stage. The testing stages are carried out by the black box testing method. This research resulted a student participation management information system that implements gamification.

articleTitle: Library Entry Access System with Body Temperature Measurement and Facial Recognition Using the Viola-Jones Method Based on a Single Board Computer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Libraries must be easily accessible to visitors. Every visitor who comes must be detected and recognized for security and comfort. The COVID-19 pandemic has ended and is now entering an endemic period, but in a new phase, this disease still poses a threat. Therefore, people need to be careful about infectious disease outbreaks and practice healthy and clean living habits. One way is to measure the visitor's body temperature before entering the library. This paper aims to improve data security when granting entry access to visitors by detecting and recognizing faces and measuring body temperature without contact. The portal will open if the system can detect and recognize the visitor's face and has a normal body temperature of around 36-37.5°C. To detect visitors' faces, the Viola-Jones method is used, which has a high level of accuracy and fast computing, while to recognize faces, the LBPH (Local Binary Pattern Histogram) algorithm is used. The LBPH algorithm is a new technique from the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) method to change the performance of facial recognition results. The system is designed using a non-contact temperature sensor MLX90614 which is used to measure body temperature, a Raspberry Pi 4 model B camera to capture visitors' faces, a servo motor to open entry access, and a Raspberry Pi 4+ as a processing and control center. The research results show that face detection is very dependent on light intensity and the distance at which the object is taken. Optimal face detection using the Viola-Jones method with the BPPH algorithm is at a light intensity of 95–120 lux with a distance of 20–50 cm, At a distance above the face is difficult to detect. Likewise, the duration of time to recognize a face, the greater the distance between the visitor and the camera, the longer the process of recognizing the face will even not be recognized at all. The system can open the portal by moving the servo motor by 55°C and the green LED lights up if the face is detected and recognized and the temperature is detected as normal.

articleTitle: Website Quality in Using the Halal Network International (HNI) Information System: Testing of Users' Attitudes, Online Co-Creatoion Experience, and eWOM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Halal Network International (HNI) is a company that manufactures a range of herbal products, providing a diverse selection of items, each of which has benefits and advantages. supported by management activities in the Online System, thereby ensuring accountability and accessibility for every Agent and Leader doing business at HNI-HPAI. In its implementation, the hni.net website experienced several obstacles, such as some of the menus available on the hni.net service which were deemed ineffective in its implementation. This research aims to understand in depth user desires for the Halal Network International (HNI) information system and identify areas of improvement that can improve the quality of the website. With the modified WebQual model, it includes ease of use, information quality, interactivity, web design, users' attitude, intention to use, online co-creation experience, eWOM. This study involved 102 participants as research subjects, with data processing conducted using SmartPLS Version 3.0 for PLS-SEM. Out of the 8 hypotheses proposed, all eight were validated, showing significant impacts.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Innovation in Public Water Utilities: A Strategic Approach with Business Intelligence Dashboards
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Public water utilities face increasing pressure to enhance operational efficiency, ensure environmental sustainability, and elevate customer experiences. In response, many utilities turn to Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards as a transformative solution. This study examines the impact of a comprehensive suite of BI dashboards, including those focused on customer relations, water usage, revenue management, penalty tracking, clustering, and forecasting, aiming to tackle prevalent challenges and unlock the full potential of BI in water resource management. Employing the BI Roadmap methodology, encompassing phases such as justification, planning, analysis, design, construction, and testing, the researchers delve into the effectiveness of these dashboards. Results indicate that BI dashboards significantly enhance analytical decision-making and resource management efficiency. Nevertheless, deploying BI dashboards requires overcoming obstacles such as data integration, stakeholder education, and system interoperability. This research offers actionable insights and practical recommendations for water utilities seeking to leverage BI dashboards to foster sustainable water governance and harness the strategic advantages of BI in their pursuit of excellence.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization Based on Analyzing Observed Wi-Fi Access Point Logs Using ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Argent demands regarding indoor real-time localization systems (RTLS) accelerate research and developments on these technologies. Recent advances in Wi-Fi technologies, including Wi-Fi 6 and 7, further facilitate the development of RTLS technologies by utilizing signal processing and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) technologies. These research and development activities also accelerate future wireless communication for achieving the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) concept. The recent developments in Wi-Fi technologies have led to increased numbers of APs for gaining reliable wireless links. Therefore, we observe many APs in workplaces, office environments, and homes. These situations enable exploiting observed Wi-Fi information for localizations. This paper proposed an indoor localization method based on the analyses of surrounding Wi-Fi access points using ChatGPT. The experiments validated that ChatGPT could infer the corresponding room names to given unknown Wi-Fi logs based on analyzing known Wi-Fi logs observed in priori in individual rooms.

articleTitle: Miniaturization and Bandwidth Enhancement of UWB MIMO Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel, miniaturized Ultra-wideband Multiple Input Multiple Output (UWB MIMO) antenna design with increased bandwidth for wireless applications. The proposed antenna comprises four elliptical-shaped monopole patch antennas inspired by the traditional Minangkabau house architecture, along with a ground plane incorporating L-shaped strips to minimize inter-element mutual coupling. Comprehensive simulations are employed to investigate the antenna's impedance matching characteristics, inter-element isolation, radiation pattern, envelope correlation coefficient, diversity gain, realized gain and total active reflection coefficient. The results demonstrate that the proposed antenna exhibits an operational bandwidth from 2.2 GHz to 20.6 GHz, with a low mutual coupling level below -20 dB, an envelope correlation coefficient < 0.02, a total active reflection coefficient (TARC) < 10 dB, and a gain of 3.5 dBi. These favorable performance metrics indicate the suitability of the proposed antenna for various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Estimating SoC and SoH of Li-ion Battery Using Coulomb Counting Method in IoT Node Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: In this research, monitoring of the battery pack is calculated by using the Coulomb Counting (CC) method based on the Internet of Things (IoT) by the state of charge (SoC) parameter as an indicator of battery capacity and state of health (SoH) as lifespan which represents the ability of the battery to store and deliver energy. SoC is the ratio of the remaining energy to the maximum energy capacity of the battery which is usually expressed as a percentage from 0% to 100%. Common terminologies used to represent battery capacity are nominal capacity—according to the datasheet—and typical capacity—calculated based on real-world conditions—using the INA219 sensor to read current (I) and voltage (V). The system designed and integrated with a 3S Battery Management System (BMS) can operate for ±22.964 hours with a SoC of ±78.85% at a voltage of 8.83V, based on a current load of ±89.28mA, and with a coulomb efficiency of 0.99. The battery monitoring system can prevent over-discharge and limit the Deep of Discharge (DoD) at ±20.15% with a C-Rate of 0.034C based on the current load. The voltage drops gradually which is relatively stable between 12V to 10V. However, there is a significant voltage drop when the battery pack voltage is below 10V and goes until the end of time. From this DoD value, it will produce more than ±10000 life-cycles of battery SoH Value which determines the life of the battery cells. Even when it reaches ±4500 cycles the energy that can be maintained is still ±75% of its maximum capacity. The SoC and SoH parameters obtained can be used as a reference for replacing the battery before it causes malfunctions in the Node devices in the IoT system being built.

articleTitle: Model Base Design of MIMO Transmitter and Receiver Implementation on an FPGA Board
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of the MIMO transmitter and receiver on an FPGA: Zynq UltraScale + MPSoC ZCU102 FPGA board. An HW/SW co-design environment designed and implemented the MIMO system on the FPGA board. The workflow including Matlab Simulink and Vivado converted a Simulink design to a Verilog HDL design. Codes for channel estimation and zero forcing operation block enabled the MIMO system. The transmitted IQ signals were loopbacked as IQ receiver signals inside the FPGA board. The designed MIMO system was implemented on the FPGA board to experimentally demonstrate the proposed MIMO system. The results verified that the MIMO system worked well on the FPGA board.

articleTitle: Rice Variety Classification via Deep Learning: Unveiling InceptionV3 and Xception Pretrained Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The classification of rice varieties stands as a crucial task in agricultural research due to its implications for food security and sustainable agriculture. Leveraging advancements in deep learning, this study compares the effectiveness of InceptionV3and Xception models in discerning various rice varieties using transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques. The research employs the Rice Image Dataset, comprising 75,000 images across five rice varieties, to train and evaluate the models. After meticulous preprocessing and model training phases, the performance of each model is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score. Results indicate that the Xception model, particularly after fine-tuning, achieves the highest accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score values, approximately 99.81%. This underscores the importance of fine-tuning in enhancing model performance for rice variety classification tasks. Therefore, the Xception model emerges as the most suitable choice for accurately classifying rice varieties, offering valuable insights for agricultural applications. Moreover, the analysis of experimental results highlights the critical role of nuanced model selection and fine-tuning techniques in optimizing classification accuracy for agricultural datasets. Ultimately, these findings contribute to the advancement of precision agriculture and underline the novelty of employing deep learning techniques for rice variety classification.

articleTitle: POSIT Arithmetic Hardware Implementation for Neural Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Nowadays, intense matrix multiplication is widely used in the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Systolic Array Matrix Multiplier, a 2D pipelined array of Processing Elements (PE) beneficial for faster and more efficient computations. In addition to this, the Posit Floating Point Standard provides better precision, wider dynamic range, and improved handling of zero and infinity which can be a promising replacement for the IEEE-754 Floating Point Standard. In this paper, an efficient 5-stage pipelined architecture for Posit Adder and Posit Multiplier Arithmetic and implemented the arithmetic on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> systolic array matrix multiplier to show its efficiency and usefulness in efficient and intense matrix multiplication applications. The model is implemented using Verilog-HDL and verified on 45nm ASIC platform and Artix-7 FPGA device (xc7a35tcpg236-1). The proposed posit multiplier has 23.49% less LUT utilization. The systolic array matrix multiplier has achieved a maximum accuracy of 99.99% for the Posit (32,2) and (32,4) configurations. The proposed architecture can be applied in intense matrix multiplication for CNN applications and many other mathematical operations.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Antenna and Repeater Node for Reading Arrayed RFID Sensor Tags in Shielded Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Collecting temperatures inside shield areas is a technological challenge for RFID sensor tags. This paper proposes a new RFID sensor tag reading technique inside shield areas such as metallic cases. The proposed method consists of an auxiliary antenna and repeater RFID sensor tag. A coaxial cable connects the repeater RFID sensor tag installed inside a shield area to the external auxiliary antenna. An RFID reader identifies multiple RFID sensor tags installed inside the shielded area through the repeater RFID sensor tag exploiting electromagnetic coupling effects. Experimental results using the chassis of a desktop computer validated that the proposed method identified the multiple RFID sensor tags and enabled measuring temperatures inside the metallic shield area.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Approach with OpenNMT for Indonesian to Gayo Language Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The Gayo language has been used by the Gayo community for approximately 7,500 years, but its usage has been continuously declining, and its digital documentation is minimal. To address this challenge, various efforts are necessary to document, preserve, and develop the Gayo language to keep it relevant for future generations. Machine translation is an automated process that converts text or speech from one language to another using computer algorithms without involving human translators. Machine translation can be utilized to revitalize regional languages through its documentation function. This research conducts an experiment by training a Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model using the OpenNMT framework and transformer architecture to translate Indonesian into Gayo. A parallel corpus was collected from the Indonesian-Gayo II Dictionary and through preprocessing steps, including case folding and punctuation removal. The dataset was divided into three parts: training data, validation data, and test data. Data augmentation was performed to increase the variation and size of the training dataset. The experimental results showed an accuracy rate of 90% for the augmented training data, with a BLEU score of 79.90. This research is an initial step in developing an NMT model for the Gayo language. The model's prediction results indicate high accuracy when the input sentences match the corpus, but are less accurate if the input sentences contain words not present in the corpus.

articleTitle: Performance of CA-Polar Codes Serial Concatenated with RLL Code Using SCL-SGRAND on VLC
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding (GRAND) algorithm is a well-established hard-decision technique that achieves maximum likelihood (ML) decoding performance. A recent variant, Soft-GRAND (SGRAND), can utilize soft information as input and is applicable to various short, high-rate block codes. We propose a scheme called successive-cancellation list (SCL)-SGRAND, where SCL decoding is employed to generate both soft information (reliability estimates) and initial hard bit decisions. These decisions are then improved using SGRAND when they fail to satisfy the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) condition. This combined approach allows SCL-SGRAND to outperform both the original SCL and SGRAND decoders. To evaluate its performance, we compare SCL-SGRAND's performance on CRC-aided Polar (CA-Polar) codes, serially concatenated with Run-Length Limited (RLL) codes (a common configuration for Visible Light Communication (VLC)), against SCL decoding and SGRAND under identical channel conditions (e.g., AWGN channel). The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SCL-SGRAND scheme outperforms both SCL and SGRAND, achieving gains of between 0.2 and 1 dB for bit error rate (BER) and between 0.3 and 0.6 dB for block error rate (BLER).

articleTitle: Two-Factor Authentication Using Face and Number-Plate Recognition for a Secure Campus Entry System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: As a public educational institution, the Universitas Andalas campus is accessed by anyone with different objectives. They have problems securing campus assets from irresponsible parties by limiting access to the campus environment. Pass cards are a physical verification for those entering and leaving the campus environment. Its card is given when entering and returning when leaving campus. However, it can still be manipulated and even cheated by irresponsible individuals. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a layered authentication system to verify every campus visitor. The face and number-plate of the vehicle used are essential parameters that can be used to validate visitor identity. This research proposes verifying faces and vehicle number-plate to improve campus security. The verification system was developed with a web-based application using the Face Recognition and EasyOCR methods supported by the Haar Cascade Classifier model as an object detection algorithm. The development method adopted is the Prototype method. The implementation consists of analysis stages, prototype design, prototype design evaluation, implementation, testing, and system evaluation. The results obtained are a web-based application prototype equipped with 2-factor authentication consisting of face and number-plate recognition as a solution offered on the Universitas Andalas. Testing was conducted on eight different visitors with different role identities, and it found that 5 of the eight facial recognition and number-plate tested did not match.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Coexistence of 802.11 WLAN and 5G Networks using a Multi-Task Learning with Convolutional Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The increasing need for high-speed internet for wireless devices has driven the development of 5G New Radio (NR) technology. The 5G NR operates in various spectrums such as sub-1 GHz, sub-6 GHz, and millimeter wave (mmWave) in the 26–28 GHz range. Conversely, the new standard Wi-Fi 6E operates on the unlicensed band and currently utilizes 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz. The coexistence of 5G NR sub-6 GHz and Wi-Fi 6E networks can result in interference and reduced performance for both technologies. To address this challenge, we introduce a Multi-Task Learning (MTL) approach using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to improve the coexistence of 5G and Wi-Fi 6E networks. This proposes identifying and classifying packets transmitted and its modulation over both types of networks. The MTL-CNN model is trained to classify packets based on their type (e.g., 5G or Wi-Fi) and to identify the specific protocol used within each packet. We confirm the accuracy of this method with Wi-Fi and 5G signals produced by the MATLAB waveform simulator and subsequently deploy it on a hardware testbed using SDR. Our experimental results show that this method improves the accuracy of packet identification and classification, thus enhancing the coexistence between 5G and Wi-Fi 6E networks. MTL-CNN potentially leads to more efficient use of the wireless spectrum and improves the overall performance of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Water Levels Changes Detection Using Millimeter Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Water levels changes detection requires a high level of accuracy. The detected data is intended to see changes in rivers or sea sites to reduce the impact caused by flooding. The manual method is still used to monitor water level changes. Several studies have also studied change detection using non-contact sensors (e.g., ultrasonic sensor). However, these existing methods still have limitations in their implementation. Detection of water level changes using millimeter wave Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar with the phase detection method produces higher accuracy. The detection is obtained by combining the peak Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with the phase value. This study uses a replica of a river that can control the water level changes. Experiments conducted in this research can detect an average accuracy rate of 93.29%. The variation of the water level changes also can be seen in this study. This method makes it possible to measure changes in water levels accurately.

articleTitle: The Light Intensity Control System and User Distance Detection on the Laptop Stand
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The use of laptops is now increasingly widespread. However, many still need to realize that using laptops with inappropriate attitudes and lighting can cause fatigue and damage to the eyes. Using a laptop for a long time can cause overheating, which will affect the laptop's performance. Therefore, in this study, a system has been created in the form of a multifunctional laptop stand that warns the user to adjust the distance from the laptop to a minimum of 46cm using an ultrasonic sensor. This system is also capable of measuring and meeting light requirements when using a laptop with a BH1750 sensor and PID control to control the intensity of light emitted by the LED with a setpoint value of 200 lux. Another capability of this system is to cool the laptop using a dc fan based on the temperature detected by the DHT22 sensor with a maximum laptop temperature of 35°C. Determination of the PID constant using the trial-and-error method with the results of Kp = 0.35, Ki = 0.18, and Kd = 0.05. The research results from the design and functional system work well in carrying out all its functions, so overall, it shows that the success rate reaches 100%.

articleTitle: Vertical Aeroponic Precision Farming Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Food farming will become a challenge as the human population multiplies rapidly while the expansion of land for agriculture at a slower rate. Urban farming, where agricultural activities are carried out in the city area, is inevitable. However, people in urban areas can use technology, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), to perform farming activities while still having a regular job. Moreover, precision farming is also possible with the help of IoT effortlessly. This paper proposes a precision vertical aeroponic farming design based on the Internet of Things. The IoT system maintains all the plant growth parameters, such as water, light, temperature, pH, and nutrient solution concentration. The IoT also controls the water irrigation in the vertical farm. The proposed system shows that aeroponic farming can be carried out with minimum direct supervision and achieve better growth by 22.5% compared to conventional agriculture.

articleTitle: Analysis of User Satisfaction on the Ticket.com Application Using the Delone & McLean Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The tiket.com mobile app functions as an online platform for travel services, akin to an Online Travel Agent (OTA). This application has service features such as booking transportation tickets, hotels or villas, as well as tickets for certain events which can help users when traveling to a place. However, in its implementation, several problems were still found in the tiket.com application, namely the absence of payment invoices, short payment limits, hotel services that were not in accordance with the application, unilateral cancellation of hotel and ticket reservations, and a refund system that made it difficult for users, causing users to providing complaints and decreasing satisfaction ratings from users. Therefore, this research aims to analyze user satisfaction with the Tiket.com mobile application and test what variables can influence user satisfaction with the Tiket.com application. The model used in this research is the Delone & Mclean model by adding the trust system variable. Using a purposive sampling technique, 125 respondents were selected to be the research sample. The results of this research show that the 10 hypotheses are acceptable and have a significant effect, with the highest T-Statistics score of 8.4682 with a regression coefficient of 0.5773 on the system reality variable which has an influence on use.

articleTitle: Proposed Design of Incubator for Fermented Soybean Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: In the process of fermenting soybeans to produce tempeh, temperature and humidity are factors that influence the quality of tempeh. A common problem encountered when producing tempeh is how to maintain the temperature so that the fermentation process of tempeh does not take too long which is related to the quality of tempeh. Furthermore, the ripeness level of tempeh during the fermentation process can be determined by its color. Tempeh that has not been fermented is still a brown soybean seed, while tempeh that has been fermented is white. So it is necessary to monitor the color of tempeh during fermentation to know when the process has finished more precisely. In this study, a soybean fermentation incubator design was proposed to produce tempeh which can regulate temperature and humidity to get the more stable temperature in the fermentation process. The PID control method is used to control the temperature in order to maintain temperature stability during fermentation. Then, the color sensors are used to check the ripeness of tempeh with an IoT-based approach. This system design propose can provide the information on the ripeness level of tempeh and receive comments via an application from a smartphone so that the temperature during the fermentation process can also be adjusted by the user.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Article Regarding Virtual Reality in Education for 2018–2023
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This bibliometric study examines the use of virtual reality (VR) in education from 2018 to 2023. The aim is to identify the main topics, authors, journals, most cited articles and relevant countries. This research uses the literature review method by analyzing 127 articles using Vos viewer and Biblioshiny. The results show that Spain and China are the leading contributors. Three main clusters of countries associated with VR in education are identified. The conclusion highlights the potential for further research, particularly in primary and secondary education and in developing countries. Despite the limitations of Scopus database data, the use of tools such as Vos viewer facilitates broader research avenues from sources such as Web of Science, Lens, PubMed, and Dimensions. This research lays the groundwork for further exploration of VR in education.

articleTitle: The Causality Model of Indonesia Rupiah Exchange Rates, Imports, and Exports Using Multivariate Time Series Model of Vector Autoregressive
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Macroeconomic indicators influence each other in the causal relationship between the rupiah exchange rate, imports and exports. Time series studies with multivariate macroeconomic data can be modeled using a vector autoregressive approach. The data used in this research are series of monthly data of exchange rate, export, and import of Indonesia starting from January 2016 to July 2022. Data stationarity was detected through the Augmented Dickey Fuller (ADF) test with the optimal lag determined using the Akaike Information Criteria (AIC) which states there is a significant short-term effect of two lags in this model. This can also be seen from the Impulse Response Function (IRF) which tends to fluctuate only in the initial lags. Based on the results of the Granger causality test, only one significant relationship can be obtained, where the increase in exports is followed by an increase in imports. This condition indicates that the volume of import and export still does not have a strong influence on the rupiah exchange rate. Meanwhile, based on variance decomposition, it shows that each variable's causality is dominantly only influenced internally by the variable itself, while the influence of other variables is still very small.

articleTitle: Node Selection Bayesian Inference MODWPT Method for EEG Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: EEG signals are inherently complex and subtle, reflecting intricate brain activity patterns. However, the presence of noise can significantly impact the quality of EEG signals and the accuracy of the information derived from them. Noise in EEG encompasses various sources, including inherent noise in electronic devices, with thermal noise being a fundamental limitation that can obscure the clarity of EEG recordings. This study focuses on the critical task of denoising EEG signals to enhance their quality and facilitate more accurate analysis. It explores the application of denoising techniques, specifically Maximum Overlap Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (MODWPT), to address the challenges posed by noise in EEG data. One of the limitations is the node selection. In order to improve this limitation, we propose a new Bayesian MODWPT. For greater accuracy, we utilize simulation signals and EEG datasets. The results conclusively illustrate the effectiveness of this approach in accurately extracting vital signal feature information while effectively filtering out unwanted noise components. This enhances the quality and reliability of EEG signal analysis in neurological research and clinical applications. This method represents a promising advancement in the field, offering improved signal fidelity and paving the way for more accurate and robust insights into brain activity and neurological conditions.

articleTitle: SambalChain: Revolutionizing the Indonesian Chili Paste Supply Chain through Blockchain for Enhanced Traceability and Authenticity
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The Indonesian chili paste market, vital to both local and global cuisines, faces challenges such as adulteration, counterfeiting, and quality inconsistency that jeopardize consumer health and reduce market trust. Traditional supply chain management methods fail to adequately address these issues due to their fragmented nature and lack of robust traceability. To overcome these hurdles, this paper introduces SambalChain, a novel blockchain-based system designed specifically for the Indonesian chili paste industry. SambalChain utilizes Hyperledger Fabric to create a secure, decentralized platform that ensures the traceability and authenticity of each spice, which is crucial for preserving the unique characteristics and quality of chili paste. This system enhances transparency by documenting every transaction on the blockchain, from spice procurement to final product distribution. Using smart contracts, SambalChain automates compliance with food safety regulations, quality checks, and payment processes, significantly reducing the potential for fraud while improving operational efficiency. This paper details the architecture and the implementation of SambalChain, demonstrating its impact on the chili paste supply chain. Performance tests indicate that blockchain integration slightly increases response times, particularly under high-load conditions, significantly enhancing product traceability and security. It concludes with discussions on potential applications of this model in other sectors of Indonesian agriculture, aiming to set new standards for food safety and transparency.

articleTitle: Smart IoT System for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Training: Embedded Sensor Integration and Android Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Lack of awareness and experience in CPR often discourages individuals from initiating rescue actions of Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This research presents a new approach to CPR training using embedded system-based devices. This system, which resembles the human body's torso and head sections, monitors and calculates key parameters critical to successful CPR, including compression, airway management, and breathing techniques. Sensor nodes are placed to measure pressure during compression and monitor airway and respiratory processes. The collected data is transmitted and processed using Internet of Things (IoT) technology with a multi-user Android application, facilitating collaborative training sessions. Experimental testing validated the system's functional capabilities with successful network connection, real-time data transmission, and effective execution of CPR procedures. Hardware implementations use microcontrollers and sensors, with Arduino and NodeMcu ESP8266 enabling data processing and transmission. Software components developed within the Arduino IDE and Android Studio ensure efficient data handling and visualization. The results highlight the system's effectiveness in improving the accessibility and affordability of CPR training, potentially improving intervention by witnesses, and improving OHCA survival rates.

articleTitle: Classification of Single Tuition Fee with Imbalanced Data Using XGBoost and SMOTE
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Tuition fees at the nation's public universities in Indonesia are determined using a Single Tuition Fee (STF) system, which aligns educational costs with students' family economic capabilities. However, the current STF group determination process, involving manual verification of various data points (parental income, number of siblings, electricity bills, etc.) for each student, is not only time-consuming and inefficient but also prone to human error due to the sheer volume of data to be processed. This research proposes the integration of technology, specifically Machine Learning, to enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and reliability of this process. We utilize the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to process and analyze data related to students' economic capabilities and other relevant variables, combined with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance issues in the data. Our approach significantly improves the F-score from an initial 0.7506 to 0.9214 and achieves an F-score of 0.8563 when tested on a different dataset, demonstrating the model's robustness and generalizability. This approach not only streamlines the STF determination process but also reduces the risk of errors, contributing to a more equitable and accessible higher education system in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Application of Collaborative Filtering and Explainable AI Methods in Recommendation System Modeling to Predict MOOC Course Preferences
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Unquestionably, the creation of MOOCs has transformed education by making learning accessible and inexpensive for people all over the world. However, consumers frequently find it difficult to select a course that fits their needs and interests due to the vast curriculum that MOOCs offer. This paper describes how a recommendation system that applies the Collaborative Filtering approach can be used to address these kinds of problems. This paper proposes a recommendation system modeling for MOOC platforms that allows users to be recommended courses based on their preferences. Using user interactions and choices, the Collaborative Filtering approach suggests courses that are specifically tailored to everyone. Utilizing a user-based method called collaborative filtering, users' preferences are predicted by comparing them to other users. The recommendation system's transparency and interpretability are improved by the incorporation of XAI using LIME. By gaining understanding of the reasoning behind course recommendations, users can build trust and make well-informed decisions. A quantitative assessment of the prediction accuracy is provided by the recommendation system's performance evaluation utilizing the RMSE measure. Over time, this statistic aids in system improvement and raises the caliber of course recommendations.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing ERP Adoption in the Hospitality Industry: A TOE Framework Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The hospitality industry has ample opportunities to enhance operational efficiency through IT systems, pivotal in transforming business operations over the last two decades. Despite the benefits, challenges like outdated systems, integration gaps, and environmental uncertainties persist. Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems offer integrated solutions for seamless operations and data sharing across organizations. However, ERP implementations often face hurdles from managerial comprehension and user resistance. Moreover, slow technology adoption and external factors like political and economic issues complicate matters. This study examines ERP acceptance in the hospitality sector, focusing on hotel management at PT XYZ's client. Using the TOE framework, a questionnaire was administered to 89 users to explore how technological, organizational, and environmental factors influence ERP adoption. The results underscore the considerable influence of technological, organizational, environmental, and individual factors on ERP adoption. The goal is to improve adoption rates in the hospitality industry by effectively balancing these technological, organizational, and environmental elements.

articleTitle: Development of Blended Learning Model Based on E-Learning and Augmented Reality in Computer Network Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This study aims to develop a Blended Learning Model based on E-learning and Augmented Reality on Computer Network Courses that is valid, practical and effective. This type of research is Research and Development, the methods and development procedures are adopted from ADDIE model. Blended Learning model based on E-Learning and Augmented Reality consists of 6 steps: (1)Learning Initial Orientation; (2) Use of Information Content and Material; (3) Tax of Group Discussion to Analysis Problem; (4)Focus Group Discussion; (5)Implementation to Present the Result of Problem Solving; (6)Evaluation. The data validity analysis used Aiken's V calculations for product validation. Practicality and effectiveness tests were carried out on lecturers and students in the form of a questionnaire. Hypothesis testing on effectiveness using independent sample t-test analysis. The findings of this study are a Blended Learning Model based on E-Learning and Augmented Reality in Computer Network Courses. The development of this model is supported by model book products, Computer Network textbooks, lecturer manuals, student manuals, application manuals, e-learning media, and augmented reality applications. The results of the product validity analysis indicate that all the products in this study are valid. The results of the practicality analysis by lecturers and students show that everything is practical. And based on the effectiveness test of this model it can improve student learning outcomes. And the implication of this research is that the Blended Learning Model based on E-learning and Augmented Reality which is developed can improve student learning outcomes in Computer Network Courses

articleTitle: Development of A Web-Based Application for the Classification of Baby Cries with A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Communication is a way of conveying ideas, views, and messages through various mediums, such as words, gestures, pictures, and symbols. All living things communicate in their own way, as babies do by crying. Crying is how babies communicate their needs and feelings to parents. However, new parents often find it challenging to understand the cries because they sound similar. Not understanding a baby's cry can lead to increased loudness and duration, impacting parents' physical and mental health. Therefore, this research proposes the development of web applications to classify baby cries using deep learning techniques. The web application was chosen to ensure flexibility, allowing it to be easily accessed on both mobile devices and computers. The model was constructed using the Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) algorithm for feature extraction in sound signal processing, and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for classifying audio from baby crying data. The dataset was obtained from an open dataset on Kaggle. The model's best performance resulted in the following f1-scores: belly pain at 64%, burping at 59%, discomfort at 57%, hunger at 64%, and tiredness at 50%. The implementation of web apps in this study can perform voice classification with file upload and audio record features.

articleTitle: Transforming Public Service: AI Chatbot Integration in SI-PEKA Mobile App Development
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its integration into chatbot applications have opened new opportunities for enhancing government administration and public services. However, developing and maintaining chatbots poses significant challenges due to the necessity of proficiency in machine learning and natural language processing, distinguishing it from conventional software development. To address these challenges, this paper introduces SI-PEKA, an innovative public service mobile application featuring the intelligent chatbot, Tanya Jaksa, integrated with advanced AI technology. By leveraging the GPT-4 assistant, facilitated by the OpenAI Platform API, SI-PEKA overcomes these development hurdles, ensuring precise and accurate responses without requiring extensive expertise in AI from developers. Currently, public service delivery at the Public Prosecutor's Office in Pekanbaru is conducted manually. SI-PEKA revolutionizes this process by offering AI-driven legal consultations, thereby enhancing efficiency and convenience for the public. This paper details the development, implementation, and testing of SI-PEKA, highlighting its transformative potential in public service delivery. The development process includes system analysis and design, application implementation, chatbot integration, testing, and iterative improvement. The application underwent rigorous Blackbox testing, achieving a 100% acceptance rate. Results indicate that SI-PEKA functions effectively, providing accurate responses to user queries and demonstrating its efficacy in addressing user needs. This study underscores SI-PEKA's role in driving innovation and adapting to the rapid advancements in AI technology to meet evolving user requirements.

articleTitle: An LDA Analysis for Topic Modeling of the RESTI Journal
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This research applies latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) modeling to uncover and analyze key topics and trends in the RESTI journal (Rekayasa Sistem dan Teknologi Informasi) journal from 2018-2022. A corpus of 594 articles was compiled and preprocessed to extract keywords/phrases. An optimized 10-topic LDA model clustered articles based on abstract texts. Quantitative and qualitative techniques analyzed the resulting topics, proportions, dynamics, and relationships. Image classification, social modeling, student systems, service applications, and digital studies emerged as dominant themes. Topic modeling revealed dramatic uptrends in AI and computer vision, mirroring explosive progress in deep learning. Disciplinary trends quantified shifts toward core computer science along with declines in social science and education. Keyword frequencies traced the rapid emergence of AI terminology. The demonstrated framework that combines metadata analysis, probabilistic topic modeling, temporal topic dynamics, and keyword trends provides a robust methodology to longitudinally analyze knowledge landscapes from research corpora. Computational analytical approaches fill a gap by showcasing versatile techniques for uncovering latent semantic patterns and research trajectories from scientific publications, offering novel tools for mapping the evolution of research themes over time. Beyond the specific context of RESTI, the presented text mining methodology has broad applications to reveal insights from diverse cross-disciplinary publication archives.

articleTitle: Assessing the Efficacy of Artificial Neural Networks for Diabetes Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The escalating prevalence of diabetes has become a significant global health concern, affecting approximately 425 million individuals worldwide by 2020. This chronic noncommunicable disease poses substantial risks to public health, particularly in aging populations, where 19.3% of individuals aged 65 to 99 were reported to have diabetes in 2019. To address this challenge, machine learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising tools for diabetes detection and risk prediction. In this context, our research explores the application of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in predicting diabetes risk, focusing on different configurations of neuron units within a single hidden layer. Leveraging the rich dataset from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), our study evaluates ANN models with 5, 10, 15, and 20 neuron units, aiming to identify the optimal configuration for accurate diabetes risk prediction. Through meticulous analysis, our findings reveal consistent performance across different neuron unit configurations, with the 15-neuron unit model demonstrating the highest accuracy of 84.863%. This suggests that the model with 15 neuron units is most effective in accurately classifying instances of diabetes, underscoring its potential for improving diabetes risk prediction.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Islamic Worship Applications on Google Play Store using Naïve Bayers Classifier and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: This research addresses the rapid increase in adherents of Islam which is directly proportional to the rapid development of technology so that of course Muslims need an application that can help with daily worship activities, one of which is the Muslim Pro application. Muslim Pro has to take user feedback into consideration in order to enhance the application's functionality. It is important to note that the majority of negative review requests will occur in 2023 and 2024. Some of the customer issues that can be found in the reviews section include a lot of annoying ads, frequent error-prone prayer alerts, accounts that are automatically logged out, upgrades that are increasingly problematic, and so forth. Sentiment analysis of user evaluations of the Muslim Pro app on the Google Play Store is the primary goal of this study. In order to categorize user opinions into three groups: negative, neutral, and positive. this study applies the Naïve Bayers Classifier (NBC) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms on a dataset of 995 reviews. The SMOTE technique is also used for data sampling. When K-Fold Cross Validation with k-10 is applied to enhance the validation findings, the SVM algorithm outperforms the NBC method, achieving an accuracy of 78% compared to the NBC algorithm's 69%. In addition to offering insights on how users see the Muslim Pro application, this study assesses the performance of the NBC and SVM sentiment analysis algorithms.

articleTitle: A Proposed Mala-Net CNN Algorithm for Malaria Early Detection Based on Thick Blood Smear
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Malaria has spread worldwide since the early 20th century and causes nearly half a million deaths each year. Malaria is actually not a dangerous disease and can be easily cured if the treatment can be carried out effectively. Therefore, efforts to identify the presence of the plasmodium parasite early will greatly help reduce the death rate caused by this disease. However, the fact is that this disease often does not get serious attention. Generally, this disease is only treated in the critical phase because it is considered just a common flu. This research is intended to produce a computer-aided disease diagnosis (CAD) system enriched with CNN algorithms to assist in early malaria diagnosis. This CAD system is expected to provide an effective and reliable malaria diagnosis, and avoid the limitations of manual diagnosis. In order to develop the CAD applications, this study proposed a novel CNN architecture called as Mala-Net by utilizing red thick blood dataset. In conclusion, this study successfully surpassed previous studies used as benchmarks with an accuracy value above 97%.

articleTitle: Optimizing K-NN Algorithm for Breast Cancer Diagnosis: A Focus on Chebyshev and Minkowski Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Breast cancer represents a significant global health concern, being the most common cancer in women and a leading cause of cancer-related deaths. Early detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes, underscoring the need for effective diagnostic tools. Machine learning techniques offer promising avenues for enhancing breast cancer detection, with the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm showing remarkable performance. This study investigates the efficacy of two distance metrics, Chebyshev and Minkowski, within the KNN algorithm for breast cancer diagnosis. Using a dataset sourced from Kaggle, comprising various tumor characteristics, the study evaluates KNN models with different numbers of neighbors (1–15) using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. The results demonstrate that the Minkowski distance consistently outperforms the Chebyshev distance across all neighbor settings, with an average accuracy of approximately 95.39%. The best-performing model is achieved using the Minkowski distance metric with 3 neighbors, exhibiting an average accuracy of approximately 96.49%. This research not only contributes to the advancement of machine learning applications in medical diagnostics but also underscores the pivotal role of algorithmic optimization in improving healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Social Identity Analysis of Small and Medium Enterprise Digitalization: An Interpretive Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Digitalization, the integration of information technology to optimize business operations, triggers significant socio-technical shifts within organizations. This global phenomenon offers substantial prospects for growth and innovation, especially for Small and Medium Enterprise (SME), which are vital contributors to the economy. However, despite recognizing its potential, most SMEs in Indonesia persist with traditional methods due to limited digital capabilities. The interpretive case study approach is used to address socio-technical aspects in digitalization at PT. XYZ, which is preparing for the implementation of enterprise resource planning (ERP) initiatives. Social Identity Theory (SIT) is used as a theoretical lens to help diagnose and understand a phenomenon within the organization. Semi-structured interviews with several stakeholders were conducted and transcribed to be analyzed through a series of codifications to identify themes and patterns. Based on the analysis of the interview conducted, we developed the initial findings of five various social identities that emerged. These identities shed light on the company's characteristics, perspectives, and attitudes toward digitization initiatives in pre crisis contexts. The findings highlight the potential for various social identities within organizations to act as significant barriers to the digitalization process if not effectively addressed.

articleTitle: Secure Safes Systems: Combining SSD Face Recognition with One-Time Password Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Safes are specially designed devices for securely storing and protecting documents, valuables, or money. Typically, safes are equipped with locks or digital combinations to prevent unauthorized access. Despite being designed for security, conventional safes are still vulnerable to breaking techniques such as hitting, prying, or using powerful cutting tools. Therefore, this project develops a new system to enhance safe security by implementing dual authentication through face recognition and a one-time password (OTP). This research uses the Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) method for face detection and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) for face classification. The system begins with face recognition of the safe owner, then generates and sends an OTP code input via the keypad. Test results show that the SSD method has 100% accuracy, while the SVM method achieves 87.5% accuracy. The system can generate a six-digit OTP code consisting of numbers and letters, changing every 2 minutes. The SW-420 sensor also successfully detects vibrations with a 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> success rate. All notifications from the system are sent to the user's Telegram application. The results of this study indicate that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy and has the potential to provide a supportive solution for safe security systems.

articleTitle: Temperature and Humidity Control System to Address Filament Brittleness in 3D Printers
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing, mainly 3D printing, has emerged as a transformative technology with widespread applications across various industries. Despite its advancements, filament brittleness remains a significant challenge, undermining the quality and reliability of printed objects. In order to address this challenge, this study built a specialized temperature and humidity management system specifically for 3D printing applications. The system utilizes a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control technique to regulate the temperature within the filament storage environment, mitigating the impact of thermal fluctuations and moisture absorption. The system has been carefully developed and tested to assure optimal printing conditions, exceptional filament quality, and uniform print accuracy and precision. Since hardware testing confirms minimum disparities between sensor readings and reference measurements, reliability in environmental management is ensured for optimized print outcomes. Moreover, software testing ensures the PID controller's efficient functionality by providing real-time monitoring and control capabilities. Functional testing reveals the system's effectiveness in maintaining optimal storage conditions for various filament types, improving the quality of prints, and minimizing waste. Incorporating essential components such as sensors, actuators, and user interface elements guarantees seamless operation and intuitive engagement.

articleTitle: Intention to Use e-Wallet for Mobile Payment: An Analysis Using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Payments that were formerly limited to cash can now be made via non-cash alternatives, such as e-wallets, in this digital age. These days, they are among the most popular payment options in Indonesia. Using the Unified Theory of adoption and Use of Technology, or UTAUT paradigm, this study seeks to ascertain the adoption of e-wallets in Indonesia as well as the factors influencing their use. The purpose of this study is to ascertain how utilizing an e-wallet affects an individual's behavioral intention. The survey uses a quantitative methodology and has 382 respondents who are spread throughout different parts of Indonesia. PLS-SEM SmartPLS 3 and IBM SPSS were used to evaluate regression analysis and structural equation modeling on the data. It was discovered that Effort Expectancy, Performance Expectancy, and Social Influence have a major and beneficial impact on behavioral intention. In contrast, it has been demonstrated that perceived risk, perceived cost, perceived trust, and self-efficacy are less reliable indicators of users' behavioral intention and have little bearing on it. This finding suggests that Indonesian e-wallet users behave similarly to those in underdeveloped nations in that they prioritize convenience, functionality, and social impact over aspects like risk, trust, and security.

articleTitle: Application of Internet of Things Technology in Cattle Farm Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The rapid advancement of information technology has significantly impacted livestock farming, a crucial sector for Indonesia's national development, particularly in meeting the population's nutritional needs. However, household-based cattle farming in Indonesia still relies on traditional methods, leading to inefficiencies in health and welfare monitoring. This research aims to address these challenges by integrating cost-effective accelerometer sensors for real-time monitoring of cattle behavior. The main objective is to enhance farming practices, improve productivity and environmental conditions, and empower farmers with data-driven decision-making. The methodology includes a comprehensive literature review on accelerometer data analysis, focusing on time series and frequency analysis methods. The system involves attaching GY-521 accelerometer sensors to cattle necks to collect movement data, which is then segmented into fixed-size windows and analyzed using statistical models such as ARIMA and wavelet transformation. Feature extraction methods include mean, radian, sine, cosine, and magnitude of the x, y, and z data. The results demonstrate that accelerometer data, processed through feature extraction and statistical models, can effectively detect and categorize cattle behaviors. The ARIMA model provides predictive capabilities, though further adjustments are needed to address data stationarity. Wavelet transformation offers insights into the time-frequency characteristics of the data. The research concludes that an IoT-based monitoring system using accelerometer sensors can provide a practical solution for real-time cattle behavior monitoring. However, further optimization is necessary to achieve low computational requirements and adaptability to different environmental conditions. This makes it a valuable tool for household-scale farmers in Indonesia. By enhancing cattle farming practices, this system can improve productivity and environmental conditions, and empower farmers, ultimately supporting Indonesia's national development goals, making it a valuable tool for household-scale farmers in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Denoising Malaria Color Images using Non-Local Means (NLM) Filter Based on Region of Interest
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Malaria is a life-threatening infectious disease spreading rapidly in the human body. People infected with the malaria parasite should receive immediate handling within 24 hours. Artificial intelligence (AI) assists medical experts in diagnosing malaria effectively and quickly. However, reliable classification necessitates image processing. A non-local means (NLM) filter was developed to reduce the noise in the images based on the four levels of region of interest (ROI). At low-level noise, NLM filtering using ROI outperformed NLM filtering using the average. NLM reduced noise based on the pixel of ROI. The highest performance occurred at an ROI of 75x75 pixels, with 38.40 ± 1.80 dB for PSNR, 36.27 ± 2.61 dB for SNR, 10.64 ±7.72 for MSE, and 0.94 ± 0.04 dB for similarity index. The filter depicted the greatest result in reducing Gaussian noise.

Index Terms: Pixels In The Region Of Interest

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of AHP and SAW Methods for Developing a Decision Support System (DSS) Applications for Recommending Car Driving Courses in Padang City
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The expansion of the car driving school service business in Padang has created various options for people seeking the most suitable driving course. However, this also raises uncertainties in their decision-making process. To date, most people visit the place directly, asking about package variabilities, fleet variants, instructor experiences, and related details when selecting a driving course. However, this approach proves burdensome, incurring financial and energy to find a suitable one. Therefore, one of the solutions is to create a Decision Support System (DSS) application that recommends the best car driving courses based on various locations and predetermined criteria. This DSS application was developed by comparing the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) methods. The method was selected for comparison because both approaches are considered objective enough to assist the human mindset in making complex decisions. Consequently, the analysis results that yield the highest scores will be used to develop a Decision Support System (DSS) application to recommend locations for car driving courses in Padang. It is hoped that the developed DSS application can be a reliable reference for the public when choosing the most suitable car driving course in Padang City.

articleTitle: Analyzing ERP Acceptance in the Hospitality Industry Using the TTF-ECT Model: A Case Study in Bali-Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The adoption of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in the hospitality industry is critical for streamlining operations and enhancing customer service. This study examines ERP acceptance using the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) and Expectation Confirmation Theory (ECT) models. Data collected from 80 ERP users in Gianyar and Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The findings reveal that aligning ERP systems with specific operational tasks and ensuring high-quality service are key to enhancing user satisfaction and system utilization. The results support the TTF-ECT model, indicating significant relationships between task fit, utilization, and satisfaction. High service quality also positively impacts user satisfaction and expectation confirmation. This study offers practical recommendations for management of the property and PT XYZ as ERP vendor to improve ERP implementation strategies, thereby contributing to the academic discourse on technology adoption in the hospitality industry.

articleTitle: The Development of Mobile Application for Object Recognition Based on Deep Learning to Assist People with Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: People with visual impairments often rely on tools like a white cane to assist them in their daily activities. They also use their sense of touch, hearing, and smell to navigate their surroundings. However, these tools and senses have limitations. For example, the sense of touch is ineffective for objects at a distance, while hearing and smell cannot identify all types of objects. Navigating new environments, such as unfamiliar outdoor areas, can be challenging and even dangerous for individuals with visual impairments due to the potential for collisions with moving objects. To address these challenges, our research aims to develop a mobile application that utilizes object recognition technology to assist people with visual impairments. The object recognition model is built using the SSD-MobileNet-vl architecture. Our experimental results demonstrate that the model can achieve a confidence level of more than 60% in real-time object detection. Additionally, the model's performance is influenced by the lighting conditions, with brighter conditions yielding better results than darker conditions for detecting moving objects.

articleTitle: The Model of Predicting Student Study Periods Using Neural Network Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: Navigating the accreditation landscape for study programs involves a critical assessment of various points, and students' academic progression is a key factor within this framework. This study, conducted at Universitas Jenderal Soedirman Faculty of Engineering, focuses on the intriguing dynamic where many students graduate beyond the standard timeframe. Factors contributing to such delays, including the Entry Path and repeated courses, have prompted an exploration into predictive models for student study periods. By addressing these challenges, our aim is to enhance decision-making processes and formulate effective strategies to bolster timely graduation rates. Data sourced directly from the Faculty of Engineering underwent meticulous curation, utilizing 26 out of 44 relevant attributes. Employing the Pearson method, correlations between study period attributes and other factors were examined. The raw data underwent robust pre-processing to transform it into a refined, analysis-ready format. The processed data was then subjected to a Neural Network Model. The modeling phase, executed in the Development Stage, involved experimentation with six hidden layer combinations and six model parameter combinations. The optimal model parameters were determined to feature a single hidden layer with 25 units, a learning rate of 0.05, and 500 epochs. These parameters were deemed optimal as they provided the best trade-off between model complexity and predictive accuracy, achieving the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) and ensuring robust performance across different data subsets. This systematic approach confirms the model's accuracy and generalizability, making these parameters the best choice for predicting student study periods.

articleTitle: Unityedu: Augmented Reality for Interactive Learning Media on Kepler's Laws using Unity3D Platform using Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) Method
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: In recent times, AR applications have gained prominence across various domains, leveraging the advanced capabilities of smartphone cameras and processing power. From Mobile AR games to educational tools, they present educators with the challenge of creating interactive learning materials, particularly in intricate subjects such as Physics. This study aims to address this challenge by developing an AR application designed to facilitate students' comprehension of Kepler's Laws in a more interactive manner. Using the Unity 3D platform and Vuforia Augmented Reality SDK, the application underwent compatibility testing to assess its performance across different versions of the Android operating system. Results indicated enhanced functionality with higher Android versions. Moreover, black box testing was employed to evaluate menu functionality, demonstrating a 100% success rate. This research underscores the potential of AR technology in enriching educational experiences and emphasizes the importance of rigorous testing methodologies to ensure optimal application performance across diverse platforms.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hate Speech Detection in the Indonesian Language using FastText and LSTM Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: The term hate speech encompasses communication that conveys hostility or prejudice toward individuals or groups based on specific attributes, including race, ethnicity, gender, or religion. Given the prevalence of such harmful content on major social media platforms like Twitter, it is imperative to prioritize ongoing research into automated detection methods. This study employs advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques, involving pivotal stages such as data collection, preprocessing, oversampling, fastText word embedding, and classification using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to achieve the objective. The amalgamation of fastText embeddings with LSTM classification yielded noteworthy results, with the model achieving 94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy, 92% precision, 94% recall, and a 93% F1 score. These outcomes underscore the effectiveness of sophisticated machine learning methodologies in accurately discerning and addressing the proliferation of hate speech online, particularly in the context of Indonesian-language content.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithm for Sentiment Analysis Using Word2Vec and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on COVID-19 Vaccination Program
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Symposium on Information Technology and Digital Innovation (ISITDI)
abstract: COVID-19 is still ongoing and has not disappeared until now in the community. The government has made various efforts to overcome this case, one of which is the vaccination program.
